revisions.purpose: Web-only change after 0.3.29, no version bump: the era-opening names on the Tc chart sit beside their own dots. Mercury stands on the record staircase at the far left of the plot, where the staircase guard blocked every close position an end or middle anchor could not reach either, so it was pushed out to a distant fallback at up to twenty-one pixels; the staircase is now held apart from the axis notes and captions, and the five landmark names are offered the close positions over a clear background, then the close positions over the staircase and the notes, and only then the distant ones, because a name crossing a line is easier to read as its dot's name than a clear one half an inch away and the white outline behind these names carries them over a line. Mercury is now nine pixels from its dot at every width. With the close positions taken earlier, MgB2 on a small chart could find nothing at all among the listed offsets, having twenty-five dots within seventy pixels of its own, so a last-resort sweep now searches outward from the dot in rings and takes the first opening wide enough, preferring one whose own dot is nearest. All five landmark names are placed at every width tested from 390 to 1400 pixels, with no name overlaps in 721 frames and the glow still paired exactly with the name. The data, the models and the results are unchanged.
